results.title: Nebius Raised the Rent 21%.
highlights:

ThePortablePortfolio

Sep 23, 2026

The B300 goes from $7.85 an hour to $9.50 on October 1. The H100 goes from $3.85 to $4.50. H200, $4.50 to $5.40. B200, $7.15 to $8.50. Between 17% and 21%, depending on the chip, and it is the second increase Nebius has sent its customers since May.

There is a detail in this one that I keep coming back to. The new rates went out as a note to customers. The public pricing page still showed the old numbers. You raise prices quietly when you are confident the customers you already have will pay and you would rather not hand the number to a rival or a reporter.

...

Nebius rallied around 7% in after-hours trading and closed September 18 at $223.54. IREN closed at $46.68, up 7.36% on the day, purely on the inference that scarce capacity can be re-let at higher hourly rates. CoreWeave slipped. That divergence is the interesting part, because the market spent the session sorting operators by who can actually capture a higher rate rather than marking the whole group up together.

results.title: Nvidia B200 Rental Prices Surge Toward $8 per GPU-Hour as Blackwell Compute Tightens | AI Industry Today
highlights:
Nvidia B200 rental compute is becoming more expensive again. The transaction-based Ornn index has risen to $7.77 per GPU-hour — up 17.1% in a month and the highest level in its public three-month window — while dedicated GPU clouds show a current median of $7.88. Different trackers report different absolute prices because they measure different provider and transaction sets, but the direction is consistent: flexible Blackwell capacity remains tight enough that B200 rental prices are rising even as newer accelerators begin entering the market.

...

Nvidia B200 rental prices have climbed toward $8 per GPU-hour as demand for Blackwell compute continues to put pressure on available cloud capacity. The transaction-based Ornn Compute Price Index for the B200 settled at $7.77 per GPU-hour on September 22, up 7.8% over seven days and 17.1% over the past month. The reading is the highest level in Ornn’s publicly available three-month history.

A separate measure of publicly listed on-demand pricing shows a similar level. GetDeploying’s latest weekly dataset puts the median B200 price across dedicated GPU clouds at $7.88 per GPU-hour, while major hyperscalers charge a median of $15.26. The $7.88 figure is therefore a provider median rather than a single transaction price or universal market average.

The distinction matters because GPU rental markets remain fragmented. Ornn calculates its benchmark from executed neocloud transactions using a volume-weighted methodology, while public-price trackers generally compare provider rate cards. Price of Compute, for example, showed a live on-demand median of $6.79 across five providers on September 23, with individual prices ranging from $5.43 at Massed Compute to $8.60 at CoreWeave.

Despite the differences in methodology, the datasets point in the same direction: premium Blackwell capacity remains expensive and recent transaction prices are rising. Ornn’s B200 benchmark has climbed from $6.64 per GPU-hour a month ago to $7.77, while its H200 index currently sits at $4.94 and H100 at $2.85. On a raw GPU-hour basis, the B200 therefore rents for about 57% more than an H200 and roughly 2.7 times the price of an H100.

That premium does not directly mean the B200 is more expensive per unit of useful AI work. Blackwell provides substantially higher throughput and memory capacity than Hopper-generation accelerators, so training or inference workloads that make full use of the architecture can finish with fewer GPU-hours.

...

Availability remains an important part of the pricing picture. Compute.world currently classifies B200 capacity as “booked / sales-gated,” citing constrained near-term availability at several major providers. Lambda’s public on-demand rate is around $6.69 per GPU-hour for an eight-GPU B200 configuration, while CoreWeave is listed at $8.60. Some cheaper listings exist, but immediate availability varies significantly by provider and region.

results.title: Spot GPU discounts run from 81.5% to nothing, September 2026
highlights:
On 2026-09-23 the discount on a spot GPU-hour runs from 81.5% at one provider down to nothing at another. Across the 42 spot rates we can set against the same provider’s own on-demand rate for the same card, the typical discount is 50%. The deepest belongs to Microsoft Azure’s H100 SXM in eastus; the shallowest are at Nebius, which since 2026-09-22 lists two of its cards at the same figure in both columns.

That last part is new. At 14:38 UTC on 2026-09-22 Nebius rewrote both columns of its price list in one go. Its H100 SXM spot rate went from $2.15 to $3.85 per GPU-hour, a rise of 79.1%; its L40S spot rate went from $0.74 to $1.55, a rise of 109.5%. Four on-demand rates moved in the same read, by 16.9% to 21.0%. The rate card at nebius.com/prices prints those figures.

...

On every one of the six cards the arithmetic lands in the same place. Nebius listed the H100 SXM on demand at $3.85 per GPU-hour until 2026-09-22, and $3.85 is what it now asks for the same card as spot capacity. The B300 says it plainly: $7.85 was its on-demand rate before the change and is its spot rate after it, against $9.50 on demand. Where the on-demand rate did not move at all — the L40S at $1.55, the RTX PRO 6000 at $1.80 — the spot column simply came up to meet it, and the two rates are 0% apart.

...

A spot rate is capacity the provider can reclaim, and the discount is what it pays a renter for accepting that. On 2026-09-23 the payment is not one number. For the H100 SXM alone we read 81.5% below on-demand at Microsoft Azure, 60.4% at CoreWeave in Europe, 50% at DataCrunch and 14.4% at Nebius. Nebius’s six cards sit between 0% and 17.4% below its own on-demand rate, the six narrowest spot discounts of the 42 pairs on the site.

Its H100 SXM spot rate is worth one more comparison. The Cloud GPU Price Index closed the week of September 21, 2026 at $3.97 per GPU-hour, the median on-demand rate card across 18 providers. At $3.85 the spot rate is below that median, but not by much — and unlike an on-demand rate it can be interrupted, which is the whole of what the discount is meant to buy.

results.title: Nebius Raises Token Factory GPU Inference Prices Up to 20% Starting Oct. 1 | Gate News
highlights: According to posts on X on Tuesday, Nebius is raising prices for its Token Factory managed inference platform by an average of 18.3%, effective Oct. 1. The increases target Pay-As-You-Go dedicated GPU endpoints, with high-end Nvidia configurations climbing sharply: H100 pricing rising 16% to $4.70 per hour, H200 up 19% to $5.60, B200 up 18% to $8.70, and B300 up 20% to $9.70 per hour. The move follows earlier price increases for on-demand cloud GPU rental rates. Last month, Nebius reported Q2 AI Cloud revenue surged 514% to $574.9 million, with adjusted EBITDA reaching $236.2 million.

results.title: Nebius GPU Price Hike 16-20%: What Changed (2026) | explainx.ai Blog | explainx.ai
highlights:
Nebius raised prices on its Token Factory GPU cloud offering by 16-20% — the second price increase the company has made in 2026. For anyone budgeting GPU rental costs, whether for training custom models or running inference at scale, a repeated price increase from a single provider within the same year is a more significant signal than a one-off adjustment, and worth factoring directly into infrastructure planning rather than treating as a minor line-item change.

highlights:
On Nov 12, 2026 an on-demand H100 rented from $1.95 an hour on Lium and $2.20 on Vast.ai, against $6.16 a GPU listed on CoreWeave (Nov 3). Where the cheap H100s are, which ones can be taken back mid-job, and the storage bill that keeps running after you stop.

...

The cheapest H100 you could rent on Nov 3, 2026 was $1.79 an hour, on-demand, on Vast.ai's marketplace (median $2.40 across 6 offers, our 12:20 UTC read). The cheapest managed H100s were Hyperstack at $2.50 (listed simply as "H100") and Runpod Secure Cloud at $2.89 for an H100 PCIe. The catch: Vast's floor is one host out of a handful and can be gone in an hour, the even cheaper interruptible H100s can be paused or taken back mid-job, and on both Vast and Runpod the storage keeps billing after you stop the instance. Lambda, Nebius and CoreWeave listed $3.29 to $6.16 for the same chip that day. For the price right now, see our live cloud-GPU compare page.

The cheapest on-demand H100 on Nov 3, 2026 was $1.79 an hour on Vast.ai's marketplace (median $2.40 across 6 H100 SXM offers). Interruptible H100s went lower: Vast from $0.89 and Nebius preemptible from $0.79, but Vast's docs say an interruptible instance may be paused if outbid. Enterprise clouds listed the same chip at $3.29 (Lambda PCIe) to $6.16 (CoreWeave, per GPU on an 8-GPU node). Storage is billed while an instance is stopped on Vast and Runpod, so delete what you don't need.

A reliable on-demand H100 from a managed provider cost about $2.50 to $3 an hour on Nov 3, 2026. Anything well above that buys enterprise capacity, multi-GPU nodes and contracts, not a faster chip. If you need 8 GPUs with fast interconnect for a training run, that premium can be worth it; for one card for a few hours, it isn't.

...

There are three, and they apply to the cheapest offers most.

1. Thin supply. Our Nov 3 read found only 6 rentable on-demand H100 SXM offers on Vast. The $1.79 one is a single host; once it's rented, the next price up is what you pay. That's why we show the median ($2.40) next to the floor. Check the host's reliability score before you rent.

2. Interruptible means it can stop. Vast's interruptible H100s started at $0.89 an hour on Nov 3 (median $2.40), and Nebius lists preemptible H100s "from $0.79" with a note that "Spot prices are dynamic and may increase or decrease based on available capacity". Vast's own docs say an interruptible instance "May be paused if outbid or if on-demand requested". The data stays, but the job stops until your bid wins again.

3. Storage bills after you stop. Vast's pricing docs say: "Storage charges continue even when instances are stopped. Delete instances completely to cease storage billing." Runpod's storage docs list volume disk at $0.10 per GB a month while running and $0.20 per GB a month while stopped. A stopped Runpod pod with a 100 GB volume disk is about $20 a month for nothing, by our arithmetic.

results.title: Best GPU Cloud Providers 2026: TOP 10 | TransAtlas
highlights:
Every number in this ranking comes from the TransAtlas live price database, collected on 2026-10-23 at 22:11 UTC: 410 listings across 10 GPU-specialized platforms. If you want the conclusion before the ranking, compare all cloud GPU providers for a side-by-side table of per-GPU-hour rates, spot discounts and egress fees. Here is exactly how the ranking was built, so you can reproduce or challenge it:

- Per-GPU caliber only. We compare `price / GPU-hour`. Listings quoted per instance (for example, an 8×H100 node) are excluded from the headline tables and discussed separately, because you cannot rent one GPU out of an 8-GPU instance.
- On-demand and Spot are never mixed. Spot prices appear in their own table with the interruption risk stated, per our GPU rental pitfalls guide.
- Only currently-available listings count toward "lowest price." A $0.23 B300 listing that has been unavailable for weeks is not a price: it is a stale catalog entry.
- Composite score = 50% price index + 30% breadth index + 20% availability rate. The price index is the percentile of a platform's available per-GPU minimums against all other platforms for the models it actually lists. Breadth is the number of distinct GPU models with verifiable pricing. Availability is the share of listings rentable at snapshot time.

See our RTX 5090 vs 4090 cloud rental analysis for when the extra money is actually worth it.

## 7 Nebius: Enterprise Spot Pricing

Nebius is the enterprise-grade option with the most aggressive Spot pricing we have ever verified: H100 Spot at $0.79/GPU-h, H200 Spot at $0.95, L40S Spot at $0.75, B200 Spot at $5.10, B300 Spot at $5.00: all marked available at collection time. On-demand is steeper (H100 $4.50, H200 $5.40, B200 $8.50), and the catalog is narrow at 6 models, but availability is 100% and the data profile is good. Best for large training jobs with solid checkpointing, where Spot interruption is a non-event.

results.title: $NEBIUS just hiked GPU cloud prices again — H100 / H200 / B200 / B300 up 16–20% from Oct 1. That's their second increase in three months. B300 now sits ~56% higher …
highlights:
# $NEBIUS just hiked GPU cloud prices again — H100 / H200 / B200 / B300 up 16–20% from Oct 1. That's their second increase in three months. B300 now sits ~56% higher … · 2026-09-23T00:00:00+00:00

$NEBIUS just hiked GPU cloud prices again — H100 / H200 / B200 / B300 up 16–20% from Oct 1. That's their second increase in three months. B300 now sits ~56% higher than before May.

What this really tells us: AI compute isn't getting cheaper — it's getting scarcer.
When a major GPU-cloud provider can raise prices twice in a quarter and still sell out, the bottleneck isn't demand. It's power, land, and cooling.

Every $/GPU-hour that climbs makes the case for owning your compute stronger. And the moment you own it, the game shifts from "rent" to "TCO" — where liquid cooling (CDU + dry cooler + closed-loop) decides whether your power bill eats your margin.

We're seeing more operators move cloud-first → build-own-run. The smart ones price cooling in from day one.
